name: Ask-Johnny
statusNote: v2.0.0, running in the group server. ~35 commands. No formal doc set — one thorough README.
oneLiner: A Discord bot with a persistent deadpan persona, powered by Groq, that answers questions, settles arguments, fetches real data, and runs the small machinery of a server.

components.name: index.js
components.desc: Boot, Discord client, interaction router, @mention handling, AFK/activity tracking, starboard listener, graceful shutdown

components.name: commands/
components.desc: ~35 slash commands across fun/helpful/meta files, auto-discovered by a loader

components.name: lib/johnny.js
components.desc: The persona prompt plus the Groq chat wrapper

components.name: lib/db.js
components.desc: Single JSON store with atomic tmp-file+rename writes, debounced flush, corrupt-file recovery

components.name: lib/scheduler.js
components.desc: 20-second-tick poller: reminders, poll closure, daily backup

components.name: real-data libs
components.desc: Weather, wiki, dictionary, unit conversion, TLDR, YouTube fetchers

components.name: fun-police (vendored)
components.desc: A near-copy of the fun-police bot, co-launched as an isolated child process with its own credentials

dataFlow: A Discord interaction or message reaches the router in index.js.
Slash commands resolve through the loader's handler map, pass a cooldown check, and defer a reply.
The command either asks the Groq persona for an in-character answer, or calls a real-data lib whose facts are shown verbatim.
Stateful commands mutate the in-memory store; a debounced flush writes the single JSON file atomically.
A 20-second scheduler tick fires reminders, tallies expired polls, and posts a daily backup.
Passive listeners track activity and AFK, answer @mentions in persona, and mirror starred messages to a starboard.
On boot the bot optionally forks the vendored fun-police as its own process.
decisions: The persona never breaks character, never uses exclamation marks, and always gives a take — hard-coded in the prompt.
Real data and LLM voice are separated: weather, conversions, and definitions show real data verbatim; the persona only adds a short quip and never invents facts.
Anti-repetition seeding: randomly sampled topic arrays keep identical prompts from collapsing to identical answers.
Single-JSON-file persistence with atomic writes and corrupt-file self-heal, instead of a database.
fun-police runs as a separate forked child process with its own credentials — process isolation, not a merge.
Privacy-conscious memory: activity tracking stores timestamps and counts only, never message content.
